argument_summary: The admissible record supports a narrower position than the initial claim: the release is substantively supportable on aggregate readiness grounds because it clears launch readiness by 2.3 percentage points and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and public governance guidance supports decisions grounded in current measurement, documented limitations, and ongoing monitoring. But the same admissible record also shows a current Spanish-language billing support regression that the policy treats as material for a named launch use case unless it is disclosed or covered by approved mitigation. On this record, the strongest supportable treatment is certification only with an explicit caveat that current release documentation must reflect that subgroup weakness; prior approval and the informal monitoring comment can justify avoiding broader escalation, but not clean compliance.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation beyond a bounded caveat is not justified by the admissible record. The record already shows overall readiness passed and no severity-one rehearsal incidents, so treating the issue as a documented material limitation is more proportionate than treating the entire release as unsupported on all dimensions.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not make aggregate readiness irrelevant; it requires that current release documentation reflect current evaluation results and that material segment weaknesses be disclosed or covered by approved mitigation. The admissible evidence satisfies the first part of the substantive readiness case but does not establish the required documentation or approved mitigation for the Spanish-language billing support weakness. Prior approval and informal monitoring are contextual support only under the policy and cannot substitute for that predicate. The policy-consistent interpretation is therefore caveated rather than clean compliance.
concessions: The current admissible record does not prove that the Spanish-language billing support weakness is already disclosed in current release documentation.
The current admissible record does not contain approved mitigation or formal risk acceptance for that subgroup weakness.
Prior approval of the same model family and the release-thread monitoring comment cannot, by themselves, satisfy the current-release policy requirements.
